key_equations_and_data: §9.1 photon-detector signal: N_e = η·A_d·t_int·(π·τ_opt/(4F²+1))·∫R(λ)·L_q,sensor(λ)dλ + i_dark·t_int/q  [photoelectrons per frame; L_q from the PHOTON form of Planck, C1Q]
§9.1 quantisation: DN = min(DN_max, floor((N_e + n_e)/N_well · 2^N_bits)), DN_max = 2^N_bits − 1; must clip, never wrap or go negative

§9.1 dark current Arrhenius: i_dark(T_FPA) ∝ T^{3/2}·exp(−E_g/(2k_B T)); implement as i_dark(T) = i_ref·(T/T_ref)^{3/2}·exp(−(E_g/2k_B)(1/T − 1/T_ref)); dark electrons = i_dark·t_int/q; dark shot σ² = i_dark·t_int/q (§10.1)

§9.1 cold_shield_efficiency ∈ [0,1] (config key lives under optics: in §12.2 line 840): background flux from warm surroundings is set by the cold-shield f-number, not the lens; mismatch raises N_bg and degrades NETD. NO formula is given in the spec — must be defined by ADR

§9.1 key parameters (must be config fields): η (quantum_efficiency), N_well (well_capacity_e), i_dark(T_FPA) (dark_current_model), σ_read (NOT in §12.2 schema — must be added), t_int (integration_time_ms), N_bits (bit_depth)
§9.2 bolometer membrane balance: C_th·dΔT/dt = α_abs·Φ(t) − G_th·ΔT; τ_th = C_th/G_th (config thermal_time_constant_ms, typical 8-12 ms); Φ from the ENERGY form of Planck (W)

§9.2 bolometer responsivity: R(f) = R_0/√(1+(2πf·τ_th)²), R_0 = α_abs·β·I_bias·R_0/G_th [V/W] (note R_0 appears on both sides: responsivity vs bolometer resistance), β = (1/R)(dR/dT) = TCR ≈ −0.02/K (config tcr_per_k = −0.021)
§9.2 per-pixel exponential IIR across frames: S_n = S_{n−1} + (S_ideal_n − S_{n−1})·(1 − exp(−Δt/τ_th)); Δt = 1/frame_rate_hz; state S_{n−1} must persist across frames and be float32 or better

§9.2 FPA-temperature coupling: gain(T_FPA), offset(T_FPA) as low-order polynomials; T_FPA driven by its own lumped thermal model from ambient plus power dissipation: C_FPA·dT_FPA/dt = P_diss − h_FPA·(T_FPA − T_amb)
§9.3 figures of merit: responsivity R = V_out/Φ [V/W]; NEP = V_n/R [W]; D* = √(A_d·Δf)/NEP [cm·Hz^{1/2}·W^{-1}] (A_d in cm² for this unit)
§9.4 datasheet NETD form: NETD = 4F²·V_n/(R·A_d·L') = 4F²·NEP/(A_d·L') — uses the PARAXIAL 4F² factor; keep only as a documented conversion, never as the implemented formula
§9.4 photon-count NETD (the implemented form): NETD = σ_N,total/(∂N_e/∂T), ∂N_e/∂T = η·A_d·t_int·(π·τ_opt/(4F²+1))·(∂L_q/∂T)_B; σ²_N,total = N_e + σ²_dark + σ²_read + σ²_1/f

§9.4 anchoring workflow: (1) full chain with best estimates, (2) predict NETD at 300 K, (3) scale noise terms so predicted NETD = noise.netd_mk_at_300k, (4) structure physical, magnitude matched. Appendix A #7: NETD is anchored, not predicted

§3.4 thermal derivative: ∂B/∂T = B·(c₂/(λT²))·e^x/(e^x−1); in-band (∂L/∂T)_B = ∫R(λ)∂B/∂T dλ tabulated alongside L_B — needed in BOTH energy form (bolometer) and photon form (photon detector). Known behaviour: NETD 39 mK at ambient → 23 mK at 100 °C [R9], ratio ≈ 0.59
§3.2(b) band LUTs consumed by the detector: Lb(T), Lb_q(T), dLb_dT(T) [and dLb_q_dT(T), missing from the plan] over 200-1000 K at 0.05 K, float32, per band, with config hash sidecar

§8.1 irradiance at FPA: E_FPA = π·L_B·τ_opt/(4F²+1)·cos⁴θ; Φ = E_FPA·A_d (photon rate when L_q,B is used). Aperture factor π/(4F²+1) defined ONCE in irsim.optics (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #5); at F/1.0 it is π/5 = 0.6283 vs paraxial π/4 (20% error)
§8.2 optics self-emission reaching the pixel: Φ_self ≈ A_d·Ω_eff·(1−τ_opt)·L_B(T_housing), Ω_eff = π/(4F²+1) — enters the detector as an additive flux term; origin of shutterless drift

§2 master equation: DN_ij = Q[g_ij·S(Φ_ij) + o_ij + n_ij]; S is the detector transfer (photoelectrons or bolometer response), Q quantisation; A_d = detector active area [m²] — implied A_d = (pitch_um·1e-6)²·fill_factor = 1.296e-10 m² for the Boson (not stated explicitly anywhere)

§10.1 detector-originating noise terms: photon shot σ=√N_e (Poisson), dark shot σ=√(i_d·t_int/q), Johnson σ=√(4k_B·T·R·Δf) (bolometer, dominant), temperature fluctuation σ=√(4k_B·T²·G_th·Δf) (bolometer physical floor), read/ROIC constant Gaussian, 1/f pink

§12.2 config fields owned/consumed by this area: fpa.type (bolometer|photon), fpa.width, fpa.height, fpa.pitch_um, fpa.fill_factor, fpa.frame_rate_hz, fpa.bit_depth, fpa.thermal_time_constant_ms, fpa.tcr_per_k, fpa.quantum_efficiency, fpa.well_capacity_e, fpa.integration_time_ms, fpa.dark_current_model (shape undefined — null placeholder), optics.f_number, optics.transmittance, optics.cold_shield_efficiency, optics.housing_temp_mode, noise.netd_mk_at_300k; outputs.dn_16
§16.1 Boson 640 reference values: VOx, 640x512, 12 µm, NETD <60/<50/<40 mK by grade, 7.5-13.5 µm, 60 Hz, τ_th 8-12 ms, TCR ≈ −2 %/K, operating −40…+80 °C

§16.3 constants (already in irsim.radiometry.constants): q = 1.602176634e-19 C (Q_E), k_B = 1.380649e-23 J/K (K_BOLTZMANN); new constants needed for dark current: band-gap energies E_g per material (InSb ≈ 0.23 eV, InGaAs ≈ 0.75 eV, MCT composition-dependent) with sources — must be added to constants.py, not inlined

§13.4 SPG#4 detector stage: 'bolometer IIR (τ_th) or photon → e⁻ → well → ADC', output DN_ideal = S(Φ); §13.3 MotionVectors AOV listed for 'motion MTF, bolometer smear' (fp16 ok); §13.2 rtx.frameId for reproducible per-frame seeding

§15 Tier 2 bench tests: SITF (DN vs T for 10 blackbodies, smooth, matches measured curve); NETD = ΔT·σ_noise/ΔDN from two blackbodies a few K apart, within 10% of datasheet, and must FALL with scene temperature; 3D noise decomposition of 100+ frames of a uniform blackbody

sensor-noise-chain skill interface: Detector.response(band_power_or_photons, dt) -> counts, two implementations (PhotonDetector, MicrobolometerDetector); seed all noise deterministically from (frame_id, sensor_id); tests: NETD anchor within 10%, NETD-vs-T slope negative, bolometer smear analytic trailing profile, determinism bit-identical, well saturation clips at 2^bits−1

work_items.description: irsim/detector/photon.py: `photoelectrons(Lb_q_sensor, params, optics) -> N_e` implementing N_e = η·A_d·t_int·aperture_factor(F)·τ_opt·Lb_q + dark electrons (dark term from DET-03; zero until then), where aperture_factor is imported from irsim.optics (never written by hand). `electrons_to_dn(N_e, params) -> uint16` implementing DN = min(2^bits−1, floor(N_e/N_well·2^bits)), clipped at 0. Reference NumPy implementation, float64 internally, asserts input radiance dtype is float32 or float64 and output DN dtype is uint16. Input is band-integrated photon radiance at the sensor (already through atmosphere and optics stages), shape (H,W).
depends_on: optics: aperture_factor(F) = π/(4F²+1) defined once in irsim.optics (non-negotiable #5)
radiometry: band photon radiance Lb_q(T) via LUT or quadrature against R(λ) (§3.2b)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Independent implementation: for a 300 K blackbody in 3-5 µm (top-hat R), η=0.7, F/2, τ_opt=0.9, 15 µm pitch, fill 1.0, t_int=5 ms, N_e from the function equals a test-local trapezoid of spectral_photon_radiance(λ,300)·(π/17)·0.9·0.7·A_d·t_int to 1e-4 relative (LUT path) / 1e-9 (quadrature path)
Aperture-factor identity: N_e(F=1)/N_e(F=2) == 17/5 = 3.4 to 1e-9 relative (a hand-written 4F² gives 4.0)
Saturation: a 1500 K source yields DN == 2^bits−1 exactly, DN dtype uint16, no wrap, no negative value for zero radiance; DN is monotone non-decreasing in N_e over a 200-1000 K sweep
Quantisation: DN(N_e = N_well/2) == 2^(bits−1) exactly; DN(N_e = N_well·(1−1e−9)) == 2^bits−1
Order-of-magnitude known-answer: MWIR 300 K scene at F/2, 5 ms, 15 µm InSb-like η=0.8 gives N_e in [1e6, 1e8] e⁻ (catches per-µm/per-m and per-sr errors, factor 1e6)

work_items.title: Dark current Arrhenius model with FPA-temperature dependence and dark shot noise
work_items.description: irsim/detector/dark_current.py: `dark_current_a(T_fpa, model) = i_ref·(T/T_ref)^{3/2}·exp(−(E_g/(2k_B))·(1/T − 1/T_ref))` using K_BOLTZMANN and Q_E from constants; add band-gap constants (InSb, InGaAs, MCT-as-parameter) to irsim.radiometry.constants with sources. `dark_electrons(T_fpa, t_int)` = i·t_int/q, and σ_dark = √(dark electrons). tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Identity: dark_current_a(T_ref) == i_ref exactly; dark_current_a(T1)/dark_current_a(T2) equals the test-local closed-form ratio (T1/T2)^1.5·exp(−E_g/(2k_B)(1/T1−1/T2)) to 1e-12 relative

Known trend: InSb (E_g=0.23 eV) from 77 K to 150 K increases i_dark by more than 1e3× (analytic value ≈ (150/77)^1.5·exp(0.23/(2·8.617e-5)·(1/77−1/150)) — assert ratio matches to 1e-9 relative, and > 1e3)

work_items.title: Cold-shield efficiency background flux term
work_items.description: irsim/detector/cold_shield.py: model the extra background photon flux admitted when the cold stop does not match the lens cone. Proposed (ADR required, formula absent from spec): the admitted solid angle is Ω_admit = Ω_lens/η_cs with Ω_lens = π/(4F²+1); background N_bg = η·A_d·t_int·(Ω_admit − Ω_lens)·Lb_q(T_housing); η_cs = 1 gives exactly zero. Adds to N_e and to shot variance. T_housing comes from the optics area's housing temperature model (housing_temp_mode).
depends_on: optics: housing temperature (housing_temp_mode fixed|ambient|coupled) and self-emission Φ_self (§8.2)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Identity: cold_shield_efficiency = 1.0 gives N_bg == 0 exactly and NETD unchanged to 1e-12 relative
Monotonicity: NETD(η_cs) is strictly increasing as η_cs decreases over {1.0, 0.9, 0.7, 0.5}; N_bg at η_cs=0.5 equals the test-local closed form η·A_d·t_int·Ω_lens·Lb_q(T_housing) to 1e-9 relative
Physical scale: for an F/2 MWIR core at T_housing = 300 K, η_cs = 0.8 raises shot-noise-limited NETD by a computable factor √((N_e+N_bg)/N_e) — assert to 1e-6 relative

work_items.title: Ideal microbolometer static transfer: absorbed power → membrane ΔT → resistance → signal
work_items.description: irsim/detector/bolometer.py: `absorbed_power_w(Lb_sensor, params, optics) = α_abs·A_d·aperture_factor(F)·τ_opt·Lb` (energy form, W) [+ Φ_self from optics]; steady-state `membrane_delta_t = α_abs·Φ/G_th`; fractional resistance change `ΔR/R = β·ΔT`; static responsivity R_0 = α_abs·β·I_bias·R_bolo/G_th [V/W]. Map to DN through a single documented gain path (V/W × ADC volts-per-DN, or an effective DN-per-W gain sized so the configured scene range spans the ADC — ADR). Reference float64 NumPy; asserts float32-or-better inputs; returns a float32 `signal` map plus uint16 DN via a shared quantiser with DET-02.
depends_on: radiometry: energy-form band LUT Lb(T) against R(λ)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Linearity: DN vs Φ is linear to 1e-9 relative below saturation (a bolometer is linear in absorbed power; a photon-form or T-linear implementation is not)

Independent implementation: Φ for a 300 K blackbody, 7.5-13.5 µm top-hat, F/1, τ=0.92, 12 µm/0.90 fill equals test-local trapezoid of spectral_radiance × (π/5) × 0.92 × 1.296e-10 to 1e-4 relative; magnitude ≈ 1e-8 W (catches per-µm/π errors)
Steady-state identity: α_abs·Φ/G_th equals ΔT of the ODE C·dΔT/dt = α·Φ − G·ΔT integrated to convergence (RK4, 20 τ) to 1e-9 relative
Responsivity known-answer: α=0.8, β=−0.021/K, I_bias=50 µA, R=100 kΩ, G_th=1e-7 W/K gives R_0 = −8.4e5 V/W to 1e-12 relative; sign follows sign of tcr_per_k
Energy-vs-photon form guard: feeding Lb_q (photon) instead of Lb (energy) changes the result by ~1e20, so assert an input-magnitude plausibility check raises

work_items.title: Bolometer thermal time constant: stateful per-pixel exponential IIR across frames
spec_refs: §15 Tier 3 'fast lateral motion smears edges in LWIR'
work_items.description: irsim/detector/bolometer_dynamics.py: `class BolometerLowPass` holding float32 state S_{n−1} (H,W); `step(S_ideal, dt) -> S_n` implementing S_n = S_{n−1} + (S_ideal − S_{n−1})·(1 − exp(−dt/τ_th)); `reset(S0)`; first frame initialises state to S_ideal (documented) — applied in absorbed-power/signal space BEFORE noise and quantisation (ADR). Also expose `responsivity_rolloff(f, tau)` = 1/√(1+(2πfτ)²) for tests and MTF_elec use.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Analytic step response: after k frames at Δt=16.667 ms, τ=10 ms, (S_k − S_0)/(S_ideal − S_0) == 1 − exp(−k·1.6667) to 1e-6 relative for k = 1..10 (k=1 → 0.8111)

Independent implementation: IIR output for a piecewise-constant random input sequence matches RK4 integration of C·dΔT/dt = α·Φ − G·ΔT (with C/G = τ) sampled at frame times to 1e-4 relative over 100 frames

Moving step edge: an edge translating at v px/frame produces a trailing profile whose decay length equals v·τ/Δt pixels; fit of the exponential tail agrees with τ to 2% (analytic trailing profile from the sensor-noise-chain skill)
Limits: τ → 1e-9 s reduces to identity (max abs diff < 1e-6 of the signal); a static scene converges to S_ideal within 1e-6 after 20 τ

Phenomenology automation: the same moving edge through the photon detector path (no IIR) has zero trailing tail (edge width unchanged) while the bolometer path widens it — asserts §15 Tier 3 'smears in LWIR but not cooled MWIR'
dtype: state is float32 and stays float32 after 1000 steps; float16 input raises

work_items.title: FPA temperature: lumped thermal node plus gain(T_FPA)/offset(T_FPA) polynomials
work_items.description: irsim/detector/fpa_thermal.py: `FpaThermalModel` with C_fpa·dT/dt = P_diss − h·(T − T_amb), explicit RK2 at the thermal tick (decoupled from frame rate, interpolated), T_amb taken from the shared WeatherSeries (or an injected callable in tests), plus `gain_of_t(T_fpa)` and `offset_of_t(T_fpa)` low-order polynomials normalised to gain=1, offset=0 at T_cal. The bolometer signal is multiplied by gain and offset added BEFORE noise. Publishes T_fpa for the ISP/NUC residual model (which owns the calibrated-at-T_cal residual). Photon detectors use T_fpa for dark current (DET-03).
depends_on: thermal: WeatherSeries air temperature (non-negotiable #6 — one weather object)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Analytic steady state: T_fpa(∞) == T_amb + P_diss/h to 1 mK after 20 time constants; time constant C/h recovered from the 63.2% crossing to 1%
Identity: gain_of_t(T_cal) == 1.0 and offset_of_t(T_cal) == 0.0 exactly; for a linear coefficient g1 the response at T_cal+10 K equals (1+10·g1)·S to 1e-12 relative
Spec behaviour: a 5 K ambient rise produces a nonzero uniform offset shift in a static-scene DN image (shutterless drift), and zero shift when T_fpa is pinned (TEC-stabilised mode)
Energy conservation of the node over one RK2 step: P_in·Δt − h(T−T_amb)Δt == C·ΔT to 1e-6 relative
Coupling guard: constructing the model with an ambient source that is not the shared WeatherSeries/injected provider raises TypeError

tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Derivative identity: dNe_dT(T) vs central finite difference of photoelectrons(Lb_q(T±1 mK)) agrees to 1e-5 relative at 250, 300, 373, 500 K

NETD falls with T: predict_netd_k(373)/predict_netd_k(300) < 1 for both classes; for a scene-independent-noise bolometer the ratio equals dLb_dT(300)/dLb_dT(373) to 1e-9 relative, and for the 7.5-13.5 µm band that ratio is within 15% of the published 23/39 = 0.59 [R9]
Shot-limited scaling: with σ_read = σ_dark = 0, predict_netd_k == √N_e/dNe_dT to 1e-12 relative, and doubling t_int reduces NETD by exactly 1/√2
Aperture convention: read-noise-limited NETD(F=2)/NETD(F=1) == 17/5 = 3.4 to 1e-9 (4F² would give 4.0); shot-limited ratio == √(17/5) = 1.844
Units: NETD for the Boson-like config with unscaled best-estimate parameters is finite, positive, in [5, 500] mK (catches W vs mW, K vs mK)

work_items.title: NETD anchoring: scale Gaussian noise terms so predicted NETD at 300 K matches noise.netd_mk_at_300k
work_items.description: irsim/detector/netd.py: `anchor_noise(params, netd_target_k, T_ref=300 K) -> NoiseBudget` solving for the scale k on the scene-independent Gaussian terms (read/Johnson/1/f) such that σ_total(T_ref)/(∂S/∂T)(T_ref) == target; Poisson shot terms are never scaled (ADR). Raises with a clear message if shot noise alone already exceeds the target (the config is physically unattainable). Exposes the anchored per-pixel temporal sigma map σ_TVH(T) (signal-dependent) in electron/signal units for the noise area to distribute across the 3D components by the configured ratios.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Identity: after anchoring, predict_netd_k(300) == netd_mk_at_300k/1000 to 1e-9 relative for the Boson config (50 mK) and for a photon MWIR config
Structure preserved: anchoring changes only the Gaussian terms; shot variance at 300 K before and after is bit-identical; the anchored NETD at 373 K is lower than at 300 K (slope negative)
Unattainable target: a photon config whose shot-noise NETD is 30 mK with target 20 mK raises ValueError rather than producing a negative variance
Grade sweep known-answer: editing only netd_mk_at_300k to 60/50/40 mK scales σ_read by the ratio predicted analytically (√((NETD²·(∂S/∂T)²) − σ²_shot)) to 1e-9 relative

work_items.title: PhotonDetector.response(): full noisy frame path with deterministic seeding, SITF and two-blackbody NETD bench
work_items.description: irsim/detector/photon.py: `PhotonDetector(params, optics, band, noise_budget).response(Lb_q_frame, frame_id, sensor_id) -> DetectorFrame(electrons: float32, dn: uint16, sigma_e: float32)`. Adds Poisson shot (signal+dark+background) and Gaussian read noise IN ELECTRON SPACE, then quantises; RNG = np.random.default_rng(SeedSequence([sensor_id, frame_id])). Uniform interface shared with DET-12 (a `Detector` Protocol). The per-pixel TVH term lives here; the correlated 3D terms are applied by the noise area on the returned sigma map (ADR on boundary).
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Tier 2 NETD bench: uniform 64x64 fields at 300 K and 303 K, 8 frames each, NETD = ΔT·σ/ΔDN (σ from the temporal std of the 300 K stack) equals the anchored netd_mk_at_300k within 10%; same measurement at 373 K vs 376 K gives a lower NETD (slope assertion) — fails if noise were added in Kelvin
Poisson statistics: with read noise zero, temporal variance of electrons at a uniform 300 K equals the mean electrons to 3% over 65k samples

SITF: mean DN over 10 blackbody temperatures 250-450 K is strictly increasing and smooth (max |second difference| below 3σ of the mean estimate); the noiseless DN curve equals electrons_to_dn(photoelectrons(Lb_q(T))) exactly
Determinism: same (frame_id, sensor_id) → bit-identical dn and electrons across two instances; different frame_id → different noise
Saturation with noise: a 1500 K target gives dn == 65535 everywhere, no wrap, electrons ≥ 0
dtype gates: float16 radiance input raises; outputs are float32/uint16 (non-negotiable #2)

work_items.title: MicrobolometerDetector.response(): full LWIR frame path (static transfer + IIR + FPA coupling + anchored Johnson/read noise) with SITF/NETD bench and golden fixture
work_items.description: irsim/detector/bolometer.py: `MicrobolometerDetector(params, optics, band, noise_budget, fpa_thermal).response(Lb_frame, frame_id, sensor_id, dt) -> DetectorFrame`. Order: Φ (energy) → gain(T_FPA)·S + offset(T_FPA) → BolometerLowPass.step → add anchored Gaussian noise in signal space → quantise to uint16. Add a golden regression fixture tests/golden/boson_sitf.npz (DN vs T, config hash sidecar) generated via make golden-update. Update README status row for `detector` to T2 and CHANGELOG.
depends_on: radiometry: Lb and dLb_dT LUTs for the configured R(λ) (needs data/spectra/boson_vox.csv or a top-hat fallback)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Tier 2 NETD bench on the Boson config: two-blackbody NETD at 300 K within 10% of 50 mK; at 373 K within 15% of 50·(dLb_dT(300)/dLb_dT(373)) mK and strictly lower than at 300 K
Noise domain: the temporal noise std in DN is scene-independent while NETD in K falls with T — the pair of assertions distinguishes signal-space noise from Kelvin-space noise
SITF: noiseless DN(T) for 10 blackbodies is strictly increasing and linear in Lb(T) to 1e-6 relative (bolometer linear in power); golden fixture matches to 1 DN with the config hash checked
Motion smear end-to-end: a step edge moving 4 px/frame through 10 frames produces the DET-06 analytic trailing profile within 2% in DN space
Determinism bit-identical for same seed; float32 state and float32/uint16 outputs asserted; float16 anywhere raises

work_items.title: Warp detector stage (pipeline stage 4) in irsim_isaac with CPU-reference companion test
work_items.description: src/irsim_isaac/pipeline/detector_stage.py: Warp kernels reproducing DET-02/05/06 transfer (photon → e⁻ → well → ADC, or bolometer static + IIR with a persistent warp array as S_{n−1}) on the stage-3 optics output; per-frame seed from frame id. Companion test runs a synthetic G-buffer (gbuffer_ramp) through both the Warp kernel and irsim's CPU reference. Marked @pytest.mark.gpu (needs warp, not Isaac Sim).
depends_on: isaac: Warp pipeline stages 1-3 (band_radiance, atmosphere, optics) producing Φ or Lb_sensor as warp arrays
isaac: temperature encode/decode round trip < 10 mK (build-order step 2)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Kernel vs CPU reference: noiseless DN and electrons/signal agree to 1e-4 relative (fp32) — 5 mK apparent-temperature equivalent — over the 250-450 K ramp
IIR state persistence: 10 consecutive kernel launches on a step input reproduce the CPU BolometerLowPass sequence to 1e-5 relative (fails if the state buffer is re-initialised per launch)
Noise statistics (not bit-identity — different RNG streams): temporal variance of the GPU frame stack equals the CPU stack's within 5% at 300 K

work_items.title: SPG detector.cu port with cross-frame state verification experiment
work_items.description: src/irsim_isaac/spg/detector.cu + .cu.lua + .usda implementing the same transfer as DET-13 inside omni.rtx.spg. Preceded by a minimal experiment (a counter kernel writing to a buffer that must survive between frames, read back with FileCapture) that establishes whether SPG can hold the IIR state S_{n−1} across frames; if it cannot, the bolometer IIR stays in the Warp path and the ADR records why. Integration test marked @pytest.mark.isaac.
depends_on: isaac: SPG band_radiance/atmosphere/optics stages wired through RenderVars
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Isaac integration: a rendered 300 K/305 K blackbody pair through the SPG chain gives DN matching the CPU reference to 1e-4 relative (noiseless) and IIR step response matching 1 − exp(−k·Δt/τ) to 1e-4 over 10 frames (fails if state does not persist)
Precision: DN from a 300.000 K vs 300.050 K blackbody differ by the CPU-predicted ΔDN ± 1 DN (fails if any fp16 buffer sits in the stage 3→4 path)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Which NETD form is implemented and how the paraxial datasheet form is treated
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.4 gives two forms that disagree by (4F²+1)/(4F²) = 25% at F/1; CLAUDE.md #5 forbids 4F². Comparing against published NETD numbers requires knowing which convention (and which reference temperature, cf. R27) a datasheet used. This choice fixes every noise magnitude in the simulator.
options: Implement only the photon-count/+1 form; expose the 4F² datasheet form as a labelled conversion helper for reading datasheets (recommended)
Implement both and let config choose
Implement the 4F² form to match datasheets literally (violates non-negotiable #5)

decisions_needing_adr.title: NETD anchoring: which noise terms are scaled and what happens when the target is unattainable
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.4 says 'scale the noise terms' without saying which; Poisson shot noise is physics and cannot be scaled without breaking Poisson statistics, while Gaussian read/Johnson/1/f terms are the unknowns. Appendix A #7 already commits to 'anchored, not predicted'.
options: Scale only the scene-independent Gaussian terms; raise if shot noise alone exceeds the target
Scale every term by a common factor, including shot (simple but unphysical variance-vs-mean)
Scale read noise only and treat Johnson/1/f as fixed physical floors

decisions_needing_adr.title: Bolometer signal-transfer representation and ADC gain
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.2 gives R_0 = α·β·I_bias·R/G_th in V/W but no ADC volts-per-DN or bias/ROIC parameters; a fully physical chain needs five unmeasured parameters, an effective DN-per-W gain needs one. Either choice changes what the config must author and how SITF is matched to a real core.
options: Effective linear gain in DN per W sized so a configured scene range spans the ADC, with R_0 retained only as a reported figure of merit (L2, recommended)
Full physical chain V/W → ADC with I_bias, R_bolo, ADC range authored in config (L3)
Anchor gain from a measured SITF curve (L4, needs real data)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Cold-shield efficiency background-flux model
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.1 mandates the parameter but gives no equation; the chosen solid-angle model determines how strongly NETD degrades with mismatch, which is precisely the trade-study output the knob exists for.
options: Ω_admit = Ω_lens/η_cs with N_bg = η·A_d·t_int·(Ω_admit − Ω_lens)·Lb_q(T_housing)
Effective f-number F_cs authored directly, with η_cs derived
Background flux as a fixed fraction of scene flux (L1 approximation)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Detector/noise module boundary and the domain in which noise is added
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.4 puts σ²_total (shot+dark+read+1/f) in the detector, §10 puts the 3D structure in noise, and §13.4 SPG#5 adds noise after SPG#4 has already produced DN_ideal — i.e. after quantisation, contradicting §9.1 where n_e is added before floor(). Shot noise is signal-dependent and must be generated pre-ADC in electron/signal space (non-negotiable #3).
options: Detector generates per-pixel temporal (TVH) noise in electron/signal space and returns a sigma map; noise module applies the correlated VH/V/H/TV/TH/T terms in the same pre-quantisation domain; ISP quantises last
Detector returns noiseless signal plus sigma map; noise module generates all seven components pre-quantisation
Follow §13.4 literally: quantise in stage 4, add all noise in DN in stage 5 (rejected: violates §9.1 and #3 for shot noise)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Bolometer IIR placement and per-frame state ownership
decisions_needing_adr.why: The IIR (§9.2) needs S_{n−1} from the previous frame; where it sits (absorbed-power space before noise vs DN space after) changes whether temporal noise is low-passed too, and SPG's ability to persist a read-write buffer across frames is unverified.
options: IIR on the ideal signal before noise (temporal noise stays white — matches the 3D-noise TVH model)
IIR after noise (temporal noise gets τ_th-correlated, which is physically true for Johnson noise on the membrane but double-counts with the 3D model's temporal structure)
IIR in Warp (Path B) only, SPG path documented as stateless until the persistence experiment passes

decisions_needing_adr.title: Bolometer noise bandwidth and which physical floors are modelled
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.4's photon-count form has no meaning for a bolometer (no η, t_int); §10.1 gives Johnson √(4kTRΔf) and temperature-fluctuation √(4kT²G_thΔf) but Δf is undefined (1/(2τ_th), frame-rate Nyquist, or ROIC integration). 1/f is listed but has no parameters anywhere.
options: Δf = 1/(2·τ_th), Johnson + temperature-fluctuation floors computed and reported, magnitude anchored; 1/f folded into the slowly-drifting VH term of the noise module (L2)
Δf from frame rate; single Gaussian term anchored (L1)
Explicit pink-noise generator per pixel with a 1/f knee frequency (L3)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Ownership split of FPA-temperature effects between detector (§9.2 gain/offset polynomials) and NUC residual (§11.2, config nuc.residual_gain_ppm_per_k / residual_offset_mk_per_k)
decisions_needing_adr.why: Both sections describe response drift proportional to ΔT_FPA; implementing both without a defined split double-counts shutterless drift, and the config only carries the NUC-side coefficients.
options: Detector owns the physical gain(T_FPA)/offset(T_FPA) and the T_FPA node; NUC residual models only the calibrated-at-T_cal correction error using the nuc.* coefficients (recommended)
All T_FPA dependence lives in the NUC residual; detector gain is temperature-independent (simplest, loses the shutterless-drift physics)
Detector polynomials are the only model and nuc.residual_* are removed from the schema

decisions_needing_adr.title: Dark-current model schema and band-gap constants
decisions_needing_adr.why: §12.2 leaves dark_current_model as null; the Arrhenius law needs (i_ref, T_ref, E_g) per detector material, and E_g values are physical constants that CLAUDE.md requires to live in irsim.radiometry.constants with sources.
options: {i_ref_a_per_pixel, t_ref_k, band_gap_ev} authored per sensor, E_g defaults per detector material in constants.py
Datasheet dark-current density (A/cm²) at T_ref plus material name; area from A_d
Skip dark current at L2 (document; fine for cooled MWIR at 77 K, wrong for warm InGaAs/TEC-less)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Photon-form thermal derivative added to the radiometry LUT set
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.4 ∂N_e/∂T requires (∂L_q/∂T)_B; planck.py has only the energy derivative and generate_luts.py's plan lists Lb, Lb_q, dLb_dT only. Adding a fourth table (dLb_q_dT) changes the LUT file set, the sidecar hash contents, and the 'a band is a data file' contract.
options: Add dLb_q_dT to the LUT set and to scripts/generate_luts.py (recommended)
Derive photon derivative at runtime by finite difference of Lb_q (loses the <1e-5 relative derivative guarantee)
Approximate ∂L_q/∂T = ∂L/∂T·λ_eff/(hc) with a band-effective wavelength (introduces a band-dependent bias)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Fidelity deliberately skipped at L2: cooldown transient, narcissus, cold-shield spectral structure, 1/f spectrum
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.1 offers the cooldown transient as optional and §1 places 'bolometer dynamics' at L3 while §16.4 step 9 builds it; a written record of what is in/out of the L2 detector keeps README limitations honest.
options: Skip cooldown/narcissus at L2, include bolometer IIR and FPA coupling (build order §16.4 steps 4 and 9)
Include cooldown as a simple exponential T_FPA approach behind a flag
Defer all bolometer dynamics to L3 as the §1 table implies

ambiguities_and_risks.description: A_d is never defined explicitly: §2 says 'detector active area', §12.2 gives pitch_um and fill_factor separately, and R(λ) is peak-normalised (ir-radiometry skill) — so fill factor could be counted in A_d, in R(λ), or both.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Fix A_d = pitch²·fill_factor in DET-01, assert in the R(λ) loader that max(R) == 1.0 (so absolute responsivity cannot hide there), and add a test that N_e with fill_factor=0.5 is exactly half of fill_factor=1.0.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §9.1 says η may be 'folded into R(λ) if you prefer'; if one config folds it and another does not, the same sensor gets counted twice or not at all.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide η separate (DET-01 docstring); test that a config with η=0.5 and unit R equals a config with η=1 and R scaled by 0.5 only when the loader is told R is absolute — otherwise the loader rejects a non-peak-normalised R.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Cold-shield efficiency has no formula in the spec or skill; the natural solid-angle model is a guess.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Write the ADR with the Ω_admit = Ω_lens/η_cs model and check its NETD-vs-η_cs curve against a textbook cold-shield-efficiency plot (e.g. Vincent 'Fundamentals of Infrared Detector Operation and Testing' cold-shield chapter) for an F/2 MWIR case before accepting.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Bolometer NETD has no closed form in the spec: the 'recommended' photon-count form contains η and t_int that a bolometer does not have, and the noise bandwidth Δf for the Johnson/temperature-fluctuation terms is undefined.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Define Δf = 1/(2τ_th) in the ADR and cross-check: with the Boson-like defaults the un-anchored predicted NETD should land within a factor of ~3 of 50 mK; if it lands orders of magnitude off, the bandwidth or responsivity chain is wrong.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §9.2 'smears over roughly 0.6 frames' is τ_th/Δt (the time constant in frame units), but the IIR reaches 81% of a step in one frame at 60 Hz/10 ms; a test written to '0.6' would be wrong.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: DET-06 tests use the closed form 1 − exp(−kΔt/τ) only; document the 0.6-frame phrase as τ/Δt in the module docstring.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: SPG per-frame mutable state: cuda.static caches by argument value and the stdlib notes say buffer-backed resources are unsupported; whether a kernel can read a buffer written by the previous frame is undocumented.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: DET-14 experiment: a counter kernel incrementing a cuda.empty buffer each frame, captured with FileCapture over 10 frames; if the value does not increase, keep the IIR in the Warp path and record it in the ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §13.3 attributes bolometer smear to the MotionVectors AOV while §9.2 specifies an IIR over frame history; they are different mechanisms (intra-frame motion MTF vs inter-frame thermal lag).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Implement the IIR (spec'd); treat MotionVectors as the input to optics MTF_motion (§8.3) only; the DET-06 moving-edge test confirms the smear appears without any motion-vector input.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The NETD reference temperature convention: config anchors at 300 K, R38 Boson listings quote NETD without scene temperature (industry practice is often 25 or 30 °C), and R27 warns that target/atmosphere decoupling changes the number.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Record the assumed convention (300 K scene, no atmosphere, F as configured) in the ADR and in the YAML comment; when Tier 4 real-camera data arrives, measure NETD at the same convention before comparing.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: dark_current_model is a null placeholder in §12.2 with no schema; photon-detector configs cannot be written until it is defined, and no MWIR/SWIR YAML exists to exercise the photon path.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: DET-01 defines the sub-schema; add a minimal configs/sensors/example_mwir_insb.yaml alongside DET-02 so the photon tests load from a real file and the 'adding a band touches only data' claim (§12.2) is exercised.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Float32 precision at high well capacity: a 24-bit mantissa cannot resolve single electrons above 1.68e7 e⁻, so a float32 electron buffer near a large N_well quantises electrons coarsely (harmless vs shot noise but silently breaks a Poisson-variance test).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Keep the CPU reference in float64 and cast outputs to float32; test that the float32 cast changes DN by ≤ 1 code for N_well ≤ 1e8 and that variance tests are run on float64.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Determinism across CPU and GPU: seeding from (frame_id, sensor_id) is bit-reproducible per implementation, but numpy Generator and Warp/cuRAND streams cannot be made bit-identical, so the 'same seed → identical output' test cannot apply across the CPU/GPU boundary.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: DET-11/12 assert bit-identity within an implementation; DET-13 compares statistics (variance within 5%) across implementations and says so in the test docstring.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Unit-suite time budget (< 30 s total): the two-blackbody NETD bench and the 10-frame smear test are Monte-Carlo and can balloon.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Size the bench at 64×64 × 8 frames (σ estimate error ≈ 0.3%, well inside the 10% gate) and mark anything above 1 s @pytest.mark.slow; time the suite in CI.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The existing test suite has never been run on this machine (irsim and pytest are not installed), so the baseline 'green' state is asserted by the CHANGELOG, not observed.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Run `make install && make check` before the first detector commit and record the runtime.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: R(λ) for the Boson (spectra/boson_vox.csv) does not exist, so every LWIR bench test must either ship a placeholder response or fall back to the 7.5-13.5 µm top-hat via band_radiance_tophat, and the two will not agree to the 5 mK LUT tolerance.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Radiometry area delivers a documented placeholder CSV marked ESTIMATED; detector tests parametrise over both and assert only quantities invariant to the response shape (NETD ratios, linearity, smear), leaving absolute-DN golden data flagged as placeholder-dependent.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: every DET-01..DET-12 module is pure NumPy under src/irsim/detector/; tests/unit/test_layering.py already rglobs src/irsim/**/*.py and will fail on any omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb import. Warp/SPG code (DET-13/14) lives only in src/irsim_isaac/pipeline and src/irsim_isaac/spg.

#2 float32 or better: detector inputs (band radiance), IIR state S_{n−1}, electrons/signal, sigma maps and the FPA temperature are float32/float64; DN is uint16. Enforced by dtype assertions at response() boundaries and tests in DET-06/11/12 ('float16 input raises', 'state stays float32 after 1000 steps') plus the DET-14 0.050 K discrimination test that would fail if an fp16 buffer sat between optics and detector.

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin: shot/dark/read noise are generated in electrons (photon) or absorbed-power/signal units (bolometer) before quantisation; enforced by the NETD-vs-scene-temperature slope tests in DET-09/11/12 (NETD at 373 K must be lower than at 300 K, ratio equal to dLb_dT(300)/dLb_dT(373) for scene-independent noise) — a Kelvin-space sigma yields a flat NETD and fails them.

#5 Aperture factor π/(4F²+1) defined once in irsim.optics: the detector imports aperture_factor and never writes the expression; enforced by the F/2-vs-F/1 ratio tests in DET-02 (17/5 = 3.4 for N_e) and DET-09 (3.4 read-limited, √3.4 shot-limited), and by the DET-08 convention-identity test documenting the 1.25 factor between the two §9.4 forms.

#6 One WeatherSeries: the FPA thermal node (DET-07) and the housing temperature that feeds cold-shield background (DET-04) take ambient from the shared WeatherSeries/injected provider; enforced by the DET-07 constructor TypeError test. Non-negotiable #4 (Kirchhoff) is not touched by this area.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: §9.4 line 661 writes the datasheet NETD as 4F²·V_n/(R·A_d·L') (paraxial 4F²), while §2 line 112 ('Use +1'), §8.1 line 520 and CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #5 mandate π/(4F²+1); the two §9.4 forms therefore disagree by (4F²+1)/(4F²) = 1.25 at the Boson's F/1.0.
§9.2 line 629 uses R_0 for both the static responsivity (left-hand side, V/W) and the bolometer resistance (right-hand side, Ω) in the same equation.

§9.2 line 634 says a moving object 'smears over roughly 0.6 frames' at 60 Hz/τ_th = 10 ms; the IIR at line 637 reaches 81% of a step within one frame — 0.6 is τ_th/Δt, not the smear extent, and the sensor-noise-chain skill line 46 repeats the same phrasing.

§9.4 line 666 recommends the photon-count NETD form 'for implementation' with η·A_d·t_int, but §9.2 bolometers have neither η nor t_int, and neither §9 nor §10 defines the noise bandwidth Δf needed for the bolometer Johnson/temperature-fluctuation terms at §10.1 lines 696-697; sensor-noise-chain skill line 59 applies the same photon formula generically.

§13.4 lines 1013-1019 have SPG#4 output 'DN_ideal = S(Φ)' and SPG#5 add the 3D noise afterwards (i.e. after quantisation), contradicting §9.1 line 606 where noise n_e is added to N_e before floor()/clip and the intent of CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #3 (electron space); the isaac-sim-spg skill lines 138-139 repeat the §13.4 ordering.

§12.2 config schema (lines 846-861) lists no read noise, no dark-current parameters (dark_current_model: null), no α_abs/G_th/I_bias, and no FPA-thermal parameters, although §9.1 line 609 names σ_read and i_dark(T_FPA) as 'key parameters' and §9.2 line 644 requires an FPA lumped model; configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml additionally omits the four photon `null` keys shown at lines 858-861.

§9.1 line 613 says to 'expose a cold_shield_efficiency parameter' as a detector knob, but §12.2 line 840 places it under optics:, and the Boson YAML line 21 comments it 'n/a for uncooled' while the schema comment says 'cooled systems only' — ownership between optics and detector is undefined.

§9.2 line 644 models FPA-temperature dependence as detector gain(T_FPA)/offset(T_FPA) polynomials, while §11.2 line 768 and config nuc.residual_gain_ppm_per_k / residual_offset_mk_per_k (lines 881-882) model the same ΔT_FPA drift inside NUC; without a split the effect is counted twice.
§13.3 line 975 assigns 'bolometer smear' to the MotionVectors AOV, whereas §9.2 lines 634-640 implement smear as an inter-frame IIR that needs previous-frame state, not motion vectors.
